title: Macintosh 128K / 512K
description: The original 1984-1986 Macintosh and its 512K "Fat Mac" successor -- the very first Mac models.

title: Macintosh Plus
description: The 1986-1990 Macintosh Plus, first Mac with a SCSI port and expandable RAM.

title: Macintosh SE / SE/30
description: The 1987-1991 compact Mac SE and SE/30 models, the last of the beige compact Macs before the Classic.

title: Macintosh Classic / Classic II
description: The 1990-1993 Macintosh Classic and Classic II, budget-priced compact Macs closing out the original 128K form factor.

title: Macintosh Color Classic
description: The 1993 Color Classic, the only compact Mac with a color CRT in the classic all-in-one case.

title: Macintosh II / IIx / IIfx
description: The 1987-1990 big-case Mac II family (II, IIx, IIfx) with six NuBus slots, Apple's first modular color Mac.

title: Macintosh IIcx / IIci / IIsi
description: The 1989-1991 compact-case Mac II family (IIcx, IIci, IIsi) with fewer slots in a smaller footprint.

title: Macintosh LC / LC II / LC III
description: The 1990-1993 low-cost "pizza box" LC line aimed at schools and budget buyers.

title: Quadra / Centris Series
description: The 1991-1995 Quadra and Centris lines, Apple's 68040-based modular Macs.

title: Macintosh IIvx / IIvi
description: The 1992-1993 all-metal, CD-ROM-equipped Mac II family (IIvx, IIvi), a bridge design reused by later Centris/Quadra/Power Mac models.

title: Macintosh Performa
description: The 1992-1997 Performa brand -- rebadged LC/Quadra/Power Mac hardware sold through mass retail, notorious for its confusing overlapping model numbers.

title: Macintosh LC 520/550/575/630
description: The 1993-1997 all-in-one and compact-tower LC models, heavily overlapping with Performa branding.

title: Power Macintosh
description: The original 1994-1997 Power Macintosh line, Apple's first PowerPC-based desktops (601/604 processors).

title: Power Mac G3
description: The 1997-1999 Power Mac G3, including the Blue and White G3 tower design.

title: Power Mac G4
description: The 1999-2004 Power Mac G4 tower, marketed with the "Supercomputer" G4 chip.

title: Power Mac G5
description: The 2003-2006 Power Mac G5, the last PowerPC-based Mac tower before the Intel transition.

title: Mac Pro ("Cheese Grater")
description: The 2006-2012 Mac Pro tower with perforated aluminum front, Apple's first Intel Xeon workstation.

title: Mac Pro ("Trash Can")
description: The cylindrical, black 2013 Mac Pro nicknamed the "trash can" for its shape.

title: Mac Pro
description: The 2019-present Mac Pro tower, returning to an expandable cheese-grater-style case.

title: iMac G3
description: The 1998-2003 original Bondi Blue and later fruit-colored translucent iMac G3.

title: iMac G4
description: The 2002-2004 "lamp" or "sunflower" iMac G4 with a hemispherical base and swiveling flat-panel display.

title: iMac G5
description: The 2004-2006 iMac G5, first all-in-one iMac to house the whole computer behind the display panel.

title: iMac (Intel, Aluminum)
description: The 2006-2020 Intel-based, aluminum-bodied iMac line.

title: iMac (Apple Silicon)
description: The 2021-present Apple Silicon iMac, thin colorful aluminum design with the M1 chip and later.

title: Mac mini
description: The original 2005-2010 white polycarbonate Mac mini, Apple's bring-your-own-peripherals desktop.

title: Mac mini (Unibody)
description: The 2010-2018 machined-aluminum unibody Mac mini with twist-off bottom panel.

title: Mac mini (2018 Redesign)
description: The 2018-2020 Space Gray Mac mini redesign aimed at professionals, last Intel Mac mini.

title: Mac mini (Apple Silicon)
description: The 2020-present Apple Silicon Mac mini, starting with the M1 chip.

title: Mac Studio
description: The 2022-present Mac Studio, a compact high-end desktop with M1 Max/Ultra and later chips.

title: PowerBook 100 Series
description: The 1991-1997 original PowerBook 100/140/170 laptops that established the modern laptop keyboard-and-trackball layout.

title: PowerBook 500/1400/3400/G3 Series
description: The 1994-1999 PowerBook 500, 1400, 3400c, and PowerBook G3 laptop models.

title: iBook
description: The 1999-2006 consumer iBook laptop line, including the colorful clamshell and white polycarbonate designs.

title: PowerBook G4
description: The 2001-2006 PowerBook G4, first the titanium and then aluminum professional laptop.

title: MacBook (Polycarbonate)
description: The 2006-2011 white/black polycarbonate MacBook, Apple's Intel-era consumer laptop replacing the iBook.

title: MacBook Air
description: The 2008-present MacBook Air, Apple's thin-and-light wedge-shaped laptop line.

title: MacBook Pro (Unibody)
description: The 2008-2012 unibody aluminum MacBook Pro with glass trackpad.

title: MacBook Pro (Retina)
description: The 2012-2016 Retina-display MacBook Pro, first Mac laptop without a traditional hard drive option.

title: MacBook Pro (Touch Bar)
description: The 2016-2020 MacBook Pro with the OLED Touch Bar and controversial butterfly keyboard.

title: MacBook Pro (Apple Silicon)
description: The 2020-present Apple Silicon MacBook Pro, starting with the M1 chip and the return of MagSafe/HDMI/SD in 2021.

title: MessagePad 100/110/120/130
description: The 1993-1997 original Newton MessagePad models with handwriting recognition.

title: MessagePad 2000/2100
description: The 1997-1998 MessagePad 2000/2100, the final and most refined Newton devices before the platform's cancellation.

title: eMate 300
description: The 1997-1998 eMate 300, a Newton-powered, translucent green clamshell laptop for classrooms.

title: iPod (Click Wheel)
description: The 2001-2014 iPod / iPod classic line navigated by the mechanical or touch-sensitive Click Wheel.

title: iPod mini
description: The 2004-2005 iPod mini, a smaller anodized-aluminum iPod in bright colors.

title: iPod nano
description: The 2005-2017 iPod nano, a thin flash-memory iPod across seven very different generations/designs.

title: iPod shuffle
description: The 2005-2017 iPod shuffle, Apple's screen-free, ultra-simple music player.

title: iPod touch
description: The 2007-2022 iPod touch, essentially an iPhone without cellular hardware.

title: iPhone / 3G / 3GS
description: The original 2007-2010 iPhone, iPhone 3G, and iPhone 3GS.

title: iPhone 4 / 4S
description: The 2010-2011 iPhone 4 and 4S, with the glass-and-steel design, Retina display, "Antennagate," and Siri.

title: iPhone 5 Series
description: The 2012-2013 iPhone 5, 5c, and 5s, introducing the taller screen, Lightning connector, and Touch ID.

title: iPhone 6/7/8 Series
description: The 2014-2017 iPhone 6, 6 Plus, "Bendgate," iPhone 7 (no headphone jack), and iPhone 8.

title: iPhone X Series
description: The 2017-2019 iPhone X, XS, XS Max, and XR, introducing Face ID and the notch, dropping the home button.

title: iPhone 11-13 Series
description: The 2019-2021 iPhone 11, 12, and 13 generations, introducing MagSafe and 5G.

title: iPhone 14-17 Series
description: The 2022-present iPhone 14 through 17 generations, introducing Dynamic Island and USB-C.

title: iPad (Original-4th Gen)
description: The original 2010-2012 iPad through the 4th generation, introducing the tablet category and the Retina display.

title: iPad Air Series
description: The 2013-present iPad Air, a thinner and lighter full-size iPad line.

title: iPad mini Series
description: The 2012-present iPad mini, a small 7.9-inch tablet.

title: iPad Pro Series
description: The 2015-present iPad Pro, Apple's large, high-end tablet with Apple Pencil and keyboard accessory support.

title: Marketplace Finds
description: Segments where the hosts discuss vintage Mac hardware they or listeners found for sale on eBay, Craigslist, or similar.

title: Listener Mail & Voicemail
description: Segments reading or responding to listener email, voicemail, or feedback.

title: Vintage Computer Festival / Expo Recaps
description: Recaps of vintage computing conventions and expos the hosts attended.
